cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing a letter to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2). He's barely done saying hello, and he gets right to it. In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, he makes an appeal.

cards.question: Paul appeals to the church in Corinth to agree together, so there may be no ___ among them.

cards.text: Some from Chloe's household have informed Paul about what's happening in Corinth. Paul's not even there and the news STILL finds him, while back when I was stuck in a junk drawer, my only news was whatever landed on top of me.

cards.question: Some from Chloe's household tell Paul there are quarrels among the believers in Corinth.

cards.text: People in the church are picking teams. Some say, "I follow Paul," others say, "I follow Apollos," an eloquent man who knew the Scriptures well (Acts 18:24), and others say, "I follow Cephas," that's Peter (John 1:42).

cards.question: One more group in the Corinthian church has its own line. Whose name do they say they follow?

cards.text: Paul hears all that and fires back: "Is Christ divided?" Then he puts his OWN name on the spot.

cards.question: When Paul asks the Corinthians, "Was Paul crucified for you?" the answer he expects is yes.
Paul has one more question for the Corinthians about himself. What does he ask?

answers.text: Were they baptized into his name
Did they ever meet him in person
Did they build a church for him

cards.text: Paul's got his own fan club, and he is shutting it DOWN. He looks back at who he baptized in Corinth.

cards.question: When Paul looks back at baptisms in Corinth, what does he thank God for?

answers.text: He baptized almost none of them
He baptized all of them himself

cards.text: Just Crispus, the synagogue leader who believed in the Lord (Acts 18:8), and Gaius. That way no one can say they were baptized into Paul's name.

Then Paul adds one more: he also baptized the household of Stephanas, the first converts in Achaia (1 Corinthians 16:15). Friend, the man is keeping this list SHORT, and it just grew by a whole household.

cards.question: After remembering the household of Stephanas, Paul says he's sure he baptized no one else.

cards.text: Now Paul spells out his job description. He tells them what Christ sent him to do.

cards.question: What does Paul say Christ sent him to do?
Paul says he doesn't preach with words of wisdom. Why not?

answers.text: So the cross keeps its power
So no one argues with him

cards.text: Now Paul gets to the heart of it: the message of the cross. To those who are being saved, it's the power of God, but it lands a whole different way on others.

cards.question: To those who are perishing, what is the message of the cross?

cards.text: Paul quotes the Lord's words in the prophet Isaiah (Isaiah 29:14): "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise; the intelligence of the intelligent I will frustrate." Then Paul calls roll for the wise man, the scribe and the philosopher of this age, and friend, NOBODY answers.

cards.question: Paul says God has made the wisdom of the world foolish.

cards.text: Paul says that in the wisdom of God, the world through its own wisdom did not know Him. That's like memorizing every cookie recipe ever written and never once finding the oven.

cards.question: The world didn't know God through its own wisdom. So how was God pleased to save those who believe?

cards.text: Paul says people show up with their own wish lists. Jews demand signs, and Greeks search for wisdom.

cards.question: Jews demand signs and Greeks search for wisdom. So what does Paul preach?
Paul says Christ crucified is a ___ to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles.
Paul says the people who are called are all Greeks, with no Jews among them.

cards.text: To those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God. Paul says the foolishness of God is wiser than man's wisdom.

cards.question: Paul also says the weakness of God is ___ than man's strength.
When Paul tells the Corinthians to think back to the time of their calling, he says most of them were powerful.

cards.text: And here's the twist: God doesn't pick the way the world picks. He chose the foolish things of the world.

cards.question: Paul says God chose the foolish things of the world. What did He choose them to do to the wise?

cards.text: God chose the weak things to shame the strong, and the lowly and despised things, the things that are not, to nullify the things that are. Friend, I was a 25-cent stamper at the bottom of a going-out-of-business bin, so I'm not offended, I'm ENCOURAGED.

cards.question: Why does God choose the foolish, the weak and the lowly?

answers.text: So no one may boast in His presence
So the strong will learn to serve
So the world will copy His ways

cards.text: Paul says it's because of God that they are in Christ Jesus. And Christ has become for us wisdom from God: our righteousness, holiness, and redemption.

cards.question: Paul ends with what's written about boasting: the one who boasts should boast in the ___.

cards.text: Me? I'm a stamper God pulled out of the back of a junk drawer, so all my bragging points one direction: UP. And friend, Paul is NOT done talking to Corinth, so stick around.
